title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X/S smooth; L an invertible sheaf on X. Problem: when does L admit an integrable S-connection, how unique is it, and how does its p-curvature behave in characteristic p? This is the rank-one case of the 'Chern class / connection / Cartier operation' theme announced on the previous page.

(1) Two hypercohomologies are compared. The first is H*_DR(X/S) = H*(X, Ω•_{X/S}). The second is H*(X, ¹Ω), where ¹Ω = σ_{≥1}Ω• = [Ω¹ → Ω² → ...] with Ω¹ in degree 1. The triangle ¹Ω → (O* --dlog--> ¹Ω) → O*[0] shows the following:
- Line bundles with integrable connection are classified by H¹(X, O* → Ω¹ → Ω² → ...).
- The obstruction for L ∈ H¹(X,O*) is its image c(L) = c₁^{dR,F¹}(L) ∈ H²(X, ¹Ω).

(2) Both groups are computed by the Hodge-to-de Rham ('first filtration') spectral sequence E₁^{pq} = H^q(X,Ω^p), E₂^{pq} = H^p(H^q(X,Ω•)). For ¹Ω the column p = 0 is missing (the little p,q diagram). Consequences:
- ¹E₂^{10} = Z¹ (closed global 1-forms) = H¹(X,¹Ω), with no quotient by dO.
- ¹E₂^{01} = 0.
- There is a low-degree exact sequence 0 → ¹E₂^{20} → H²(X,¹Ω) → ¹E₂^{11} → ¹E₂^{30}.
- ¹E₂^{11} = Ker(H¹(Ω¹) → H¹(Ω²)), with no quotient by dH¹(O).
- ¹E₂^{20} = E₂^{20} = closed global 2-forms / d(global 1-forms).

The map ¹Ω → Ω• gives vertical maps to the usual sequence 0 → E₂^{10} → H¹_DR → E₂^{01} = Ker(H¹(O) → H¹(Ω¹)) → E₂^{20} → H²_DR → ..., with E₂^{11} = Ker/Im.

(3) Obstruction analysis:
- (a) The image of c(L) in ¹E₂^{11} is the Hodge Chern class c₁^{Hdg}(L) = [dlog g_ij] ∈ H¹(Ω¹). This is the Atiyah class, the obstruction to any connection.
- (b) If (a) vanishes, a connection exists. Its curvature is a closed global 2-form, and changing ∇ by a global 1-form α changes it by dα. So the second obstruction is the class of the curvature in Z²/dΓ(Ω¹) = E₂^{20}.
- If both vanish, the integrable connections form a torsor under Z¹ (closed 1-forms).

(4) NB in characteristic p:
- p·c(L) = 0, since dlog(g^p) = 0. So L^{⊗p} carries a canonical integrable connection (Cartier), and the obstruction map factors through Pic(X)/p, an F_p-vector space.
- Hence the obstruction vanishes on p·Pic(X).
- Over an algebraically closed field with X proper, Pic⁰ is p-divisible, so the obstruction vanishes on Pic⁰.
- He asks (à vérifier) whether it vanishes on all of Pic^τ.

(5) p-curvature in rank one: ψ(ξ) = ∇_ξ^p − ∇_{ξ^{[p]}} is additive and p-linear V_{X/S} → End(L) = O, i.e. a section of Ω^{1(p)}. Replacing ∇ by ∇ + ω (ω closed) gives
ψ'(ξ) = ψ(ξ) + ω(ξ)^p + ξ^{p−1}(ω(ξ)) − ω(ξ^{[p]}).
By Cartier/Jacobson this equals ψ(ξ) + ω(ξ)^p − ⟨Cω, ξ̃⟩·1, i.e. ψ changes by (F* − C)(ω). The margin note reminds him to state Jacobson's formula explicitly.

Implicit goal: decide when L carries an integrable connection with ψ = 0, i.e. (Cartier descent) when L ≅ F*M. The relevant operator on closed forms is 1 − C, whose kernel gives the logarithmic forms.
errors: The bottom exact sequence is continued past H²_DR as H²_DR → E₂^{11} = H¹(H¹(X,Ω•)) → E₂^{30}. In general this is not exact or even well defined: the low-degree sequence of a first-quadrant spectral sequence stops at E₂^{20} → H². Further maps need vanishing of E₂^{0q} (q ≥ 1) or E₂ degeneration. For ¹Ω (column p = 0 empty) the analogous extension 0 → ¹E₂^{20} → H² → ¹E₂^{11} → ¹E₂^{30} is legitimate.
Vanishing of the obstruction on p·Pic(X) needs no properness: L^{⊗p} always carries the canonical connection.
Vanishing on Pic⁰ uses p-divisibility of Pic⁰(k) over an algebraically closed field, which fails over a general base S.

The Pic^τ claim is rightly marked 'à vérifier'. The p-primary part of Pic^τ/Pic⁰ need not be p-divisible, and it is not clear that its de Rham F¹-Chern class vanishes in all cases (e.g. surfaces with p-torsion in NS in char p).

Sign and normalisation in the Cartier term: the identity used is ξ^{p−1}(ω(ξ)) − ω(ξ^{[p]}) = −⟨Cω, ξ⟩^p (up to Frobenius-twist conventions). The trailing '=' shows the computation was left unfinished.

ideas.what: Obstruction to an integrable connection on a line bundle as its class in H²(X, Ω^{≥1}), analysed via the truncated Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence into (a) Hodge/Atiyah class and (b) curvature class in Z²/dΓΩ¹
ideas.modern_name: Atiyah class / F¹-de Rham Chern class; multiplicative de Rham (Deligne-type) cohomology H¹(O* → Ω^{≥1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Atiyah (1957) for connections; Deligne, Mazur–Messing, Illusie for the de Rham/hypercohomology formulation
ideas.where_published: Related material in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); not this exact computation as far as I know

ideas.what: In char p the obstruction is killed by p, vanishes on p·Pic and hence on Pic⁰ over an algebraically closed field
Change of p-curvature of a rank-one connection under ∇ → ∇ + ω: ψ' = ψ + (F* − C)ω via Jacobson's formula
ideas.modern_name: Katz's formula for p-curvature of d + ω; Cartier operator
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem, 1970, §7); Cartier

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether line bundles in Pic^τ(X/S) (proper smooth X in char p) always admit integrable connections, marking it 'à vérifier'. The p-torsion part of NS is the crux. This is answered or understood via crystalline Chern classes and torsion in H²_crys, so it is not genuinely new.
missed.quote: nulle si ξ est dans Pic^τ(X/S) (à vérifier ...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; it ties to the known question of injectivity/vanishing of c₁^{dR} on torsion of NS in char p, which the literature treats (Illusie, Ogus).

deep.surprise_reason: Standard working notes: the obstruction-theoretic description of integrable connections on line bundles and Katz's p-curvature/Cartier formula are both classical and published by 1970–79. Nothing appears beyond the literature.
transcription_corrections: ¹Ω_{X/S} is σ_{≥1}Ω• with Ω¹ placed in degree 1 ('degré 1' annotates Ω¹).
In the bottom row the arrow H²_DR(X) → H¹(H¹(X,Ω•)) is drawn as a doubled/overwritten arrow, not a clean map.
'l'obstruction de p Pic(X) l'obstruction est nulle' likely means 'que sur p·Pic(X) l'obstruction est nulle' (followed by the Pic^τ claim with 'à vérifier').
'{+Sauf car. p>0,+}' is more plausibly 'Sans car. p>0' or 'Si car p>0' inserted above 'l'indétermination'. Uncertain.
'c'est une 1-forme fermée [?] ou fermée' is likely 'c'est une 1-forme relative au fermée (dω=0)'.
Margin: 'rappeler la formule de Jacobson explicitée' (reminder to recall Jacobson's formula explicitly).
'défaut de compatibilité aux puiss. p-ièmes' is the p-curvature; v: V^{(p)}_{X/S} → End(L), here a section of Ω^{1(p)}_{X/S}.
